Daily KRW trend analysis.text:
## 🇰🇷 Won morning brief: Wed 11 Nov 2026 (SGT)

**SGD/KRW is about 1,045, roughly 105 KRW (≈10%) below your 1,150 target.** The won strengthened over the past week, which moved the rate further from your target. Last night's hot US inflation data may push it back somewhat today.

### 1. Rates
**USD/KRW**
- **1,337.5** at the Seoul close on 10 Nov, 3:30pm KST. That is **down 9.6 won** on the day and the won's second straight daily gain (Seoul Economic Daily).
- **Week:** down from **1,356.6** on 6 Nov, about **−1.4%** (won stronger). The end-of-October level was 1,334.3.
- Trading Economics showed **~1,343** later on 10 Nov, slightly weaker after Seoul closed.

**SGD/KRW: sources disagree, so treat these as a range**
- Cross rate from 1,337.5 ÷ USD/SGD 1.2818 (Trading Economics, 10 Nov): **≈1,043.5**
- XE mid-market: **1,050.62** (9 Nov, 23:03 UTC)
- Wise mid-market: **~1,034** (checked this morning, no timestamp). This is at Wise's 30-day low, and Wise shows −2.5% over 30 days.
- Korea base rate (매매기준율, collected 10 Nov): **1,060.01**, +1.59 on the day
- ⚠️ Investing.com showed **1,105.8** (−0.24% on the day, undated). It doesn't match any of the other sources, so I'd treat it as a bad quote.
- I couldn't find a reliable 1-week SGD/KRW change. USD/SGD was roughly flat over the past month, so the week was probably about −1% to −1.5%.

**Distance to the 1,150 target**
- From ~1,045: **+105 KRW (≈+10%)**
- Across sources: +90 KRW (8.5%) to +116 KRW (11.2%)

### 2. Why the won moved
- **Foreign stock flows decided the week.** Foreigners sold a net ₩10.4tn of KOSPI stocks during 2–6 Nov, about ₩7.7tn of it in Samsung and SK hynix. The KOSPI fell 11.7% that week, a circuit breaker was triggered on 6 Nov, and USD/KRW peaked at 1,356.6. On 10 Nov the KOSPI rebounded 4.4%, foreign selling eased, and the won firmed.
- **Hot US CPI overnight is dollar-positive.** October CPI rose 0.4% m/m against 0.3% expected, and core rose 0.3% against 0.2%. Markets now price about an **84% chance of a Fed hike in December**, and 15% odds of a 50bp hike. Fed Governor Waller said he leans toward a hike. The US 10-year yield is near 4.93–4.98%, and the DXY rose ~0.3% to ~102. This could weaken the won today.
- **Chip sentiment is fragile.** Nvidia fell 5.5% on 10 Nov, which could weigh on Samsung and SK hynix and keep foreign investors selling. Exporters selling dollars has cushioned the won's falls.
- **Geopolitics and oil:** Hopes for US–Iran talks and lower oil prices supported the won's gains on 10 Nov. I found no new MAS action. USD/SGD rose ~0.2% on 10 Nov.

### 3. What to watch
- **Today:** Seoul's reaction to the CPI data and Nvidia's fall. Korea's 1–10 Nov export data usually comes out around now.
- **12 Nov:** KOSPI 200 options expiry, which can bring volatility.
- **More Fed speakers** ahead of the December meeting, including Vice Chair Bowman.
- **26 Nov:** Bank of Korea rate decision, its last meeting of the year.
- **30 Nov:** MSCI index rebalancing takes effect, which can move foreign flows.

### 4. Bottom line
Short-term risks lean toward a slightly weaker won, from a firmer dollar and fragile chip stocks. Even so, 1,150 would need about a 10% move, and the won has strengthened about 14% since June. Reaching the target in the near term looks unlikely unless there's a major risk-off shock. Uncertainty is high.

_Not financial advice._

Daily AI newsletter.text:
**☀️ The Daily AI Brief — Tue, 10 Nov 2026 (SGT)**

Anthropic ships a new frontier model, Nvidia's board opens an investigation into its own CEO, and Google pushes into robots and custom silicon.

---

## Top stories

**Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2**
Anthropic released new versions of its two top models, which share one underlying model. Fable is open to everyone with tighter safeguards, and Mythos is limited to vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations. Anthropic says responses are up to 30% faster than 5.1, and it claims the model formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in about 30 hours and helped crack two open black-hole physics problems. Pricing is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with an optional fast mode that costs double. It's available on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure.
Why it matters: Frontier labs are now competing on long-running agent work and real research results, not just chat benchmarks.

**Nvidia's board investigates Jensen Huang over a possible foreign intelligence target**
After NYT reporting tied Huang to a businesswoman U.S. officials consider a Chinese intelligence asset, Nvidia's independent directors started a review with outside counsel. The board says it has no reason to think secrets were compromised and still backs Huang. Lawmakers are asking for briefings, and China calls the allegations groundless.
Why it matters: The world's most important AI chip company now faces a governance and national-security question right at the top.

**Google DeepMind unveils Gemini Robotics 2.5**
DeepMind's newest vision-language-action model improves task success by 30% to 100% over its previous baseline and finishes tasks 20% to 30% faster. In a pilot with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz, Apollo 2 humanoids kitted car parts on production lines with 96% success. DeepMind also open-sourced ASIMOV-Jailbreak, a benchmark for robot safety.
Why it matters: Humanoid robots are moving from demo videos onto real factory floors.

**Google adds two new TPU variants to take on Nvidia**
The TPU 8tx is built to keep data private while AI processes it (confidential inference), and it pairs with AMD EPYC CPUs. The TPU 8i Max packages two 8i chips together to double compute and memory bandwidth for memory-heavy work. Google hasn't announced pricing.
Why it matters: Google is filling out its own chip lineup to win enterprise inference work away from Nvidia GPUs.

---

## Quick hits

- 🛒 **OpenAI** now sells ChatGPT Enterprise through AWS Marketplace, so spending can count toward customers' AWS commitments.
- 🪶 **Meta** released Muse Ember, its smallest and cheapest Muse model, built for agent tasks like tool calls and routing ($0.10 per million input tokens).
- 🔓 **Fireworks AI** disclosed cyberattacks that exposed customer data and parts of unfinished models. Some customers are reportedly moving business elsewhere.
- 🤖 **Nvidia** launched the GR00T 2 robot model and Isaac Lab 3.0, with up to 2.5x faster training.
- 🔐 **DeepMind's AlphaProof Code** formally verified security properties of Signal's protocol code, generating over 6 million lines of Lean proof.
- 🍎 **Apple** is selling $49.99 "Intelligence Usage Packs" that add AI usage once the monthly limit runs out, starting with Logic Pro.

---

## Tool of the day

**Gemini Memory summary**: US Google AI subscribers can now see everything Gemini remembers about them, sorted by category, and edit or delete any of it. It's worth a 5-minute check to fix outdated details so answers fit you better.

---

Daily nutrition science read.text:
**🛌 The Cheapest Calorie Cut: One More Hour of Sleep**
*~2 min read*

Short sleep doesn't just make you tired. It changes how much you eat the next day, and the evidence on this is fairly consistent.

**What happens when sleep is cut short.** A 2016 meta-analysis from King's College London pooled 11 controlled studies (172 people). On days after restricted sleep, participants ate about **385 extra kcal**. They didn't burn noticeably more energy to make up for it. The studies were small and short, but they all pointed the same way.

**Why it happens.** Sleep loss shifts the hormones that control appetite: ghrelin (which drives hunger) tends to rise and leptin (which signals fullness) tends to fall. Brain-imaging studies also show that reward areas react more strongly to high-calorie food when you're tired. That's why the late-night pull towards a snack or supper feels much stronger after a short night. More time awake also simply means more chances to eat.

**The encouraging part: it works in reverse.** In a 2022 randomised trial in *JAMA Internal Medicine* (University of Chicago), 80 adults with overweight who normally slept under 6.5 hours got about **1.2 extra hours** of sleep a night, mostly after a single sleep-hygiene session. They kept living their normal lives, and intake was measured objectively with doubly labelled water. They ate about **270 fewer kcal a day** on average, without being told to diet. The trial lasted only 2 weeks, so long-term weight effects are still being studied. Still, it's one of the strongest real-world signals we have.

**Why this matters for muscle too.** When people diet on short sleep, a larger share of the weight they lose tends to come from lean mass rather than fat. That makes sleep a partner to your ~120 g protein target, not a separate project.

**What this means for you:** With your 8pm cut-off, protect your sleep window rather than fighting late-night hunger with willpower. Put your phone away about 30–45 minutes before bed and aim to sleep at a consistent time. The UChicago trial's main trick was simply limiting screens before bed. If you're still up and hungry well after 8pm, treat that as a sign you need to sleep, not a sign you need more food.

**Sources**
- [King's College London: sleep deprivation and calorie intake (meta-analysis)](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/archive/news/kings/newsrecords/2016/11%20november-/sleep-deprivation-may-cause-people-to-eat-more-calories)
- [UChicago Medicine: more sleep reduces caloric intake (JAMA IM, 2022)](https://www.uchicagomedicine.org/en/forefront/research-and-discoveries-articles/2022/february/getting-more-sleep-reduces-caloric-intake)
